newsitem.title: INDIA: India divestment should fund education, health - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India divestment should fund education, health - RBI.

text.p: Funds raised from India's divestment programme must be used to fund education and public health schemes rather than retire government debt, chief of the central bank said on Wednesday.

"So long as government is a net borrower of a fairly large magnitude year after year, it does not make any material difference whether the resources are utilised to retire past debts or simply utilised as part of receipts," Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan said.
"In the latter case, it only results in a lower borrowing requirement," he told a conference on divestment.

Rangarajan who inaugurated the one-day conference said there were two reasons for divestment of governemnt ownership in state-run firms-to provide fiscal support and to improve efficiency of the firm.

"There is a compelling need to expand the activities of the state in areas such as education, health and medicine," he said. "It is therefore legitimate that a part of the additional resources needed for supporting these activities comes out of the sale of shares."
Rangarajan said the government needed to define what companies formed "non-strategic and non-core sectors," divestment in which could be more than 51 percent under an official paper.

He said in the fiscal year 1994/95 (April-March) 130 state firms, out of total 241, made profits of 121.2 billion rupees. Of these, 10 firms accounted for two-thirds of the profits; and six of these firms were oil firms.
The losses of 109 firms aggregated 49.10 billion rupees in 1994/95, he said.
The total government investment in the 241 firms as on March 31, 1995 was 1,724.38 billion rupees.
Details of the workings in 1995/96 were not immediately available.
